lead: Overnight into Sunday: what OpenAI's math results leave out, a breach exposing coding-agent API keys, Nadella on Windows as agent territory, and a mixed bag of lawsuits, AI debt, crawler paywalls and quantum error reduction.

sections.title: OpenAI's math bounty, and what it skipped
sections.intro: A field-by-field analysis of OpenAI's 700+ published math results finds cryptography and other areas conspicuously absent - and asks whether the gaps reflect the model's limits or the lab's choices.

sections.title: The OpenCode breach and agent credentials
sections.intro: A 'large scale distillation attack' on the company behind OpenCode exposed stored OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API keys for ~1.4% of Console users - exactly the credentials a terminal coding agent runs with.

sections.title: Nadella on Windows as agent territory
sections.intro: Microsoft's CEO pairs the Nvidia RTX Spark-powered Surface Laptop Ultra with a plan to make Windows a safer OS for AI agents, whose billion-machine footprint makes it both target and host.

sections.title: Money, files and crawlers
sections.intro: OpenAI alleges a departing employee took 100+ files on an unreleased product to Apple; the NYT spots weak links in AI borrowing at CoreWeave, Oracle and SoftBank; Pay-per-Crawl ships an HTTP 402 paywall for AI crawlers on ten stacks; Google claims a 40x error reduction from magic state cultivation on Willow; and Codex Desktop's crash-dump bug gets a tracking issue.
